frames.note: Audit frames of your clip (inside your cut if you cut it): one with nothing in front of the board, one with the occluder on the board (a mask frame), the one with the strongest perspective, and one consecutive pair (f, f+1) for the temporal terms. Fill in the frame indices and model.interval before the first generation. The three named frames must be distinct and have audit corners; the occluded frame also needs an audit mask. Choose a pair mapping to distinct output frames at the model frame rate. Use the same full audit dictionary for classical and generative temporal interpolation.
frames.selection_note: Before generation, changed 258/259 to 259/260 for Wan 16 fps: former both map to output 138; new pair maps to 138/139 from source start 0. Frame 260 uses the evaluator's interpolation from the full corner audit dictionary. Other selected frames unchanged. [AI-DESIGN]

model.requirement: One open-weight video model generates the edited pixels directly. Inference scripts are permitted. One attempt, fixed settings/seed across duration-limited segments; log every segment and technical retry.
model.examples: Use an open-weight video model your hardware supports, for example MiniMax-H3 (MiniMax, 2026, https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3), JoyAI-Video-Edit (JD Open Source, 2026, https://github.com/jd-opensource/JoyAI-Video-Edit), LTX-2.3 (Lightricks, 2026, in/outpainting IC-LoRA) or Wan2.1-VACE-14B (Wan, arXiv:2503.20314; VACE, Jiang et al., arXiv:2503.07598); other open-weight models are equally welcome. Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B (Apache 2.0) is a smaller option; memory depends on settings (staff trial: 14 GB, 13 min for a 5.5 s cut at 480p, mask + reference image). The staff example with MiniMax-H3 is in data/genai_oracle/.
model.name: Wan2.1-VACE-14B (QuantStack GGUF Q5_K_M)

interval.note: Inclusive original source indices; 0.000 to 12.633333 s exclusive at 30 fps. Original 442-frame capture retained. Three consecutive segments on one global 16 fps grid; final input padding removed only from joined output, raw outputs preserved.

model.backend: ComfyUI + city96/ComfyUI-GGUF, imported from Python without UI
model.status: completed: attempt 2 (corrected VACE inpainting inputs), submitted in outputs/genai/; attempt 1 archived in outputs/genai/attempt1_mv2v/
model.settings_note: Attempt 2 settings chosen on common-clip validation only (outputs/genai_validation/), frozen before any personal-clip generation. Model, quantisation, seed, sampler, steps, CFG and shift equal attempt 1. Final run samples with a per-step CUDA synchronisation after three technical failures (non-finite segment 1), see outputs/genai/technical_failures/.

control.lost_frames: convex hull of the nearest frozen-tracker quads before and after
control.mask_source: frozen flow-assisted tracker corners only; audit annotations never given to the model

model.compute: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 16 GB, ComfyUI --lowvram, CPU text encoding; 2769.9 s for the 3 submitted segments, 11.42 GiB peak PyTorch allocation

inputs: your clip (or your cut of it)
board masks from your frozen pipeline (only if the model needs a mask)
prompt.template: Replace the poster on the board in this video with the attached artwork: a vintage travel-poster illustration of a rocky coast with a red-and-white lighthouse on a cliff, a sailboat with a red sail on a blue sea, a large red sun, seagulls in the sky and colourful flowers in the foreground.
prompt.note: Generic instruction plus a one-sentence content description of the artwork; the description was required for the reference to be used (common-clip ablation). [AI-DESIGN]

evaluation: vace_inpaint.py --clip personal_clip --evaluate --sync-steps: identical selected source indices and full audit dictionary for both classical variants, the generated output and a re-encoded source baseline; outputs/evaluation/stage4_genai_reports.json.
declaration: model name and visible version, date, settings (steps, resolution, seed), the video you gave it (whole clip, cut, or joined segments), output fps, prompt, time, compute
artwork_status: Final crop supplied by Matthew, 1481x1024; used unchanged for both methods.
